done_when: When Forge's review runs on Claude (Autoreview's Claude engine), the reviewer can read every file in the review checkout read-only, as Codex reviews can, and still cannot write or run commands that change anything. Find how Autoreview's Claude engine limits file access and change Forge's side (the arguments, environment or review folder Forge passes) to grant it; if Autoreview offers no way, say so with evidence and stop. A command-level test proves the Claude review is started with read access to the checkout.

findings.body: The pinned Autoreview helper accepts Claude Code >=2.1.169 and probes only its existing isolation flags (`ensure_claude_isolation_supported`, lines 4903–4937 of the [pinned helper](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/blob/ce14dcca09b3affb922ddcca11465619e67f5114/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview)). However, [Claude's CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) requires >=2.1.248 for `--restricted`. On versions 2.1.169–2.1.247, preflight therefore passes but this added argument makes the actual review fail with an unknown option. Forge retries and refuses close; `forge doctor` only checks Claude's presence at `src/forge/doctor.py:89–91`. Check the new minimum and provide an actionable upgrade message before launching the review.
findings.title: P2: Check the Claude version required by --restricted

why: Code reviews on Claude see only the diff: Autoreview's Claude engine gives the reviewer no access to the rest of the checkout, so in today's benchmark Claude reviews let through about half the changes that should have been blocked
